objective: Add the Records tab to the Stats page (Seasons / Records / Players): Historical, with Team and Player tabs of record cards whose holder each card shows and each of which opens that record's full ranked list as a stats navigator level, and Seasonal, the per-season leaders moved off Seasons in this same unit; retire the Stats page's copy of the table CSS.
acceptance_criteria: The Stats page's route tabs are Seasons, Records and Players, in that order, as today's Tabs; /stats/records is a lazy child route (its own chunk, like SeasonsTab and PlayersTab); /stats still redirects to /stats/seasons, and the Seasons and Players addresses and teamHref and the other helpers in features/stats/links.ts keep their output for the same inputs.

Records tab: a SegmentedTabs bar Historical / Seasonal (Historical the default). The view is ?view=seasonal in the address (Historical is the default and is not written; an unknown value shows Historical), so a reload, a shared link and Back keep it. Historical holds a second SegmentedTabs bar Team / Player (Team the default, ?group=player, an unknown value shows Team) over that group's record cards, in the order GET /events/records returns them, and one line naming the data window from its since_season and through_season ("Since 2003-04, through 2026-27"; with no window, no line). Both bars replace the history entry, as the conference bar does, rather than push one; switching the view drops group, record and season from the address.

A record card shows its title as a heading (h3), "View all" at the right of the title, and its holder: the team (name) or the player (first and last name, and for a single-game record the team they played for), the value with its unit, and the season or the game's date and opponent where the record has one; a holder tied with others says so ("and 1 other" for tied_count 2, "and 2 others" for tied_count 3); a record with no holder says nothing qualifies yet. Clicking anywhere on the card opens that record's ranked list: the card has exactly one interactive element, the "View all" link (a real address, /stats/records?record=<id>, so it can be opened in a new tab), whose accessible name includes the record's title, and whose hit area covers the whole card; the holder's name on a card is plain text (no link inside the link). Each record's rule is on its list level, not its card.

Record level: opening a card pushes a navigator level onto the Records stack, as Seasons' team level does. The record level's group is its list's group (the address is ?record=<id> and never carries group): the breadcrumb (the navigator's "Stats path") reads "Team records › <title>" or "Player records › <title>" by that group, and until the list lands its first item reads "Records"; Back and the breadcrumb's first item return to Historical on that group's tab (Back from a cold ?record=player-points-game lands on ?group=player with Player selected). A reload, a shared link and the browser's Back keep the record; an unknown id shows the API's not-found as an in-place message with the way back. Headings: the records level's h2 is "Team records" or "Player records"; a record level's h2 is the record's title, taken from the cached summary when there is one and from the list otherwise, so it is never empty after a card opens. The level shows its rule, "Since <since_season>" and its whole list (up to its top 100, total entries) in one ScrollTable: rank, the team or player (linked: a player to /players/<id>, a team to the Seasons tab filtered to it for that season through the adapter's teamLink), the team a player played for, the season or the game (its date linked to /games/<id>, and the opponent), and the value; a column the record has no value for (the team for career and championship records, the season or game for counts) is left out, so no column of blanks. Ranks are the API's as given: a season record's rows can show the same three-place percentage with different ranks, because the API ranks the exact fraction, and the list says so in one line under the table when the record is a season record. The Historical / Seasonal bar stays above the navigator; the Team / Player bar belongs to the records level and is not shown on a record level.

Seasonal: the season's leaders, moved from Seasons in this unit (the human, 2026-10-24: never a deploy without them): a season select (?season=, the newest season by default and not written, as on Seasons), then an h2 "<season> leaders", then today's Leaders section unchanged (the rule line, then the points, rebounds and assists boards); Seasons no longer renders Leaders, and nothing else on Seasons changes.

The records reads live in frontend/src/api/records.ts (fetchRecords and fetchRecord with their query keys, typed from api/schema.d.ts), with staleTime Infinity (Prompt 20 R7: the routes are cached five minutes at the edge, and the data changes once a day at most); a record's list is asked for once, at limit=100 (R11: one call shows the whole list, at most 27.5 KB); no records read passes offset.

Navigator: the record level (and the records level under it) are levels of components/stats-nav/'s StatsNavigator, so the breadcrumb, Back and the focus rule are the navigator's (focus moves to the new level's heading when a control in the navigator opens or pops a level, and not on a cold load or the browser's Back); the StatsLevel union grows, and every use narrows by kind; StatsNavAdapter grows an optional teamLink(teamId, season | null, children), without which a team's name is plain text, and features/stats/links.ts's ROUTE_LINKS gives it through teamHref; the navigator stays router-agnostic (stats-nav-lazy.test.ts's scan holds) and features/stats/ is the route adapter.

R24: the Stats page's copy of the table CSS is retired: features/stats/Stats.module.css keeps only .tab, .controls, .section, .muted and the team bar's rules (.combobox, .options), and no .scroll, .table, table-cell, .name or .figure rule; every stats table (the leaders' included) is drawn by components/stats-nav/'s ScrollTable with the navigator's own stylesheet, which gains .figure, and the leaders' cells take the navigator's classes; ScrollTable and ColumnHeader lose their classes prop if nothing else passes it. The record cards' styles live in components/stats-nav/ too.

Accessibility: both bars are UI-010's SegmentedTabs (tablist, arrow keys, one tab stop) whose panel holds what they switch; each card is a list item in a list named by its group; "View all"'s focus ring is visible and the whole card shows the hover and focus state; every table keeps its caption, column scopes and row headers; nothing on the Records tab prints null, undefined or NaN.

Every existing frontend test passes, except a test that pins the leaders on Seasons, the two route tabs, the Seasons request counts, the Stats copy of the table CSS or the only tablist on the Stats page, or whose typing breaks on the grown StatsLevel union; such a test is changed in the test commit and named in the PR body. The skeptic's prototype broke these, and each is changed in the test commit, since test edits are frozen during implementation: SeasonsTab.test.tsx (11: the leaders tests, the league view's tables x2, the season picker x2 and the season-wide games list, which wait on or ask about the leaders), stats-requests.test.tsx (all four Seasons tests: seasonLevelLoaded waits on the Leaders region), StatsPage.test.tsx (4), stats-css.test.ts (the scroll-container check for features/stats), SeasonsNavigation.test.tsx ("keeps the leaders below the standings"), TeamSearch.test.tsx ("clearing the bar returns to the league view" expects the Leaders region) and StatsNavigator.test.tsx (typecheck: level.season on the grown union).
